newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece must cut spending to contain debt growth - EU.
newsitem.headline: Greece must cut spending to contain debt growth - EU.

text.p: Greece should switch from tax collecting to reducing primary spending in order to contain its debt-to-GDP ratio and catch up with its European Union partners, a senior EU official said.

The director general of Economic and Financial Affairs at the European Commission, Giovanni Ravasio, said that despite successful steps by the Greek government to cut inflation and deficits, further effort was needed for convergence.

"Despite progress already made in nominal convergence there is considerable distance yet to cover before Greece fulfills securely the convergence criteria," Ravasio told an economic conference organised by the Economist.

Projected drops in the average inflation as measured by the GDP deflator to 6.8 percent in 1997 and 4.2 percent in 1998, were owed to a strict monetary policy, with exchange rate policies helping contain imported inflation, he said.
But with the government unable to adequately cut its spending, fiscal policy made Greece's disinflationary targets harder to meet.

Spending cuts would also help reduce budgetary imbalances, a top priority for convergence. Greece's 1996 deficit of 7.4 percent of GDP was the highest in the EU and the debt-to-GDP ratio the third highest at 111.8 percent.
"The consensus appears to be that successful adjustments are characterised by expenditure reductions rather than tax increases," Ravasio said.

He argued against further increases in taxation, saying that it had shown signs of fatigue and limited results in recent years and urged Greece to follow the lead of other EU members which are aiming to reduce both the tax burden and government spending. -- Dina Kyriakidou, Intercontinental Pressroom +0301 9206370
